import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 180

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/180](https://www.erdosproblems.com/180)
- [ErSi82] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M., *Compactness results in extremal graph theory*.
  Combinatorica (1982), 275-288.
- [OpenAI26] OpenAI, *Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science*. (2026).
-/

open Filter SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos180

/-- A finite graph, bundled with its vertex count, so that a family may mix orders. -/
structure FiniteGraph where
  order : ℕ
  graph : SimpleGraph (Fin order)

/-- A host graph is `family`-free when it contains no member of `family` as a subgraph. -/
def FamilyFree (family : Finset FiniteGraph) {n : ℕ} (host : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ forbidden ∈ family, forbidden.graph.Free host

open scoped Classical in
/-- $\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})$, the greatest number of edges of a graph on `n` vertices
containing no member of `family`. -/
noncomputable def familyExtremal (family : Finset FiniteGraph) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter (FamilyFree family)).sup
    fun host : SimpleGraph (Fin n) => host.edgeFinset.card

/-- No member of the family is acyclic. -/
def IsCyclicFamily (family : Finset FiniteGraph) : Prop :=
  ∀ forbidden ∈ family, ¬ forbidden.graph.IsAcyclic

/-- The family is *compact*: some single member already controls the family extremal number. -/
def IsCompactFamily (family : Finset FiniteGraph) : Prop :=
  ∃ forbidden ∈ family, ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      (extremalNumber n forbidden.graph : ℝ) ≤ C * (familyExtremal family n : ℝ)

/--
If $\mathcal{F}$ is a finite set of finite graphs then $\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})$ is the maximum
number of edges a graph on $n$ vertices can have without containing any subgraphs from
$\mathcal{F}$. Note that it is trivial that $\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})\leq \mathrm{ex}(n;G)$ for
every $G\in\mathcal{F}$. Is it true that, for every $\mathcal{F}$, there exists $G\in\mathcal{F}$
such that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;G)\ll_{\mathcal{F}}\mathrm{ex}(n;\mathcal{F})?$$

This is the Erdős–Simonovits compactness conjecture. The answer is no: OpenAI [OpenAI26] give a
family of connected bipartite graphs, none of them acyclic, for which no single member controls
the family extremal number. See `erdos_180.variants.counterexample`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_180 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ family : Finset FiniteGraph,
      family.Nonempty → IsCyclicFamily family → IsCompactFamily family := by
  sorry

/--
The counterexample: a nonempty family of connected bipartite graphs, none acyclic, that is not
compact.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/openai/ten-proofs/blob/94bc0feb6a9ff12c7d31d6de640a725c9d43d2b6/CompactnessAndDegeneracy.lean"]
theorem erdos_180.variants.counterexample :
    ∃ family : Finset FiniteGraph,
      family.Nonempty ∧
      (∀ forbidden ∈ family,
        forbidden.graph.Connected ∧ forbidden.graph.IsBipartite ∧
          ¬ forbidden.graph.IsAcyclic) ∧
      ¬ IsCompactFamily family := by
  sorry

end Erdos180

findings.description: The docstring at lines 60–67 presents the unrestricted historical question, but the Lean statement uses the corrected version: the family must be nonempty and every member must contain a cycle. The Lean mathematics agrees with the cited OpenAI26 paper; the prose should identify this correction. Cyclicity is not a redundant restriction: the all-forest family {K₁,₂, 2K₂} has family extremal number 1 while both individual extremal numbers grow linearly.
findings.source_evidence: OpenAI26, Chapter 10, §1.1, p. 237 (https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/ten-proofs-oai.pdf), explicitly distinguishes the original formulation from the corrected question for a 'finite nonempty family of graphs ... all of whose members contain cycles.' It gives {K₁,₂, 2K₂} as an elementary counterexample to the original formulation. Wigderson's note, pp. 1–2 (https://ywigderson.math.ethz.ch/math/static/Compactness.pdf), makes the same distinction.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the main theorem's docstring to ask about nonempty finite families whose members all contain cycles, identifying this as the corrected compactness conjecture. Optionally explain the elementary counterexample to the unrestricted version. No change to the Lean statement is needed.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses an eventual upper comparison ex(n,F) ≤ C·ex(n,𝓕), with C > 0. Wigderson's corrected formulation uses the lower comparison ex(n,𝓕) ≥ c·ex(n,F) for every n. OpenAI26 already uses the eventual formulation adopted by Lean.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under IsCyclicFamily, a graph with one edge and isolated vertices is family-free, so familyExtremal 𝓕 n ≥ 1 for n ≥ 2. Individual extremal numbers vanish at n = 0,1 and are bounded by n.choose 2. Thus an eventual comparison starting at N extends to every n after replacing C by C + N.choose 2. Taking c = 1/C converts the upper comparison into Wigderson's lower comparison, and conversely. Both equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/BoundaryChecks.lean as compact_iff_all_n and compact_iff_wigderson, without sorry.

review.notes:
No mathematical misformalization or stale status was found. The cyclic-family restriction is explicitly part of the corrected conjecture in the cited primary paper, rather than an unjustified extra hypothesis.

Lean checks established singleton agreement with extremalNumber, the family-to-member inequality, the empty-family and n = 0,1 values, attainment of the maximum for cyclic families, positivity for n ≥ 2, ordinary rather than induced subgraph semantics, and the Big-O and negated-compactness quantifiers. The inadmissible-host supremum default cannot affect either theorem.

I compiled the complete CompactnessConjecture namespace from the exact linked proof. checkedManuscriptCounterexample, not_erdos_180, and quantitativeCompactnessCounterexample depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The linked counterexample supplies the variant's stated properties under the evident transport between the two identical graph encodings. The website records the negative answer and Lean verification, matching the file's metadata.

Direct website access was blocked by Cloudflare; readable website text was obtained through the proxy, and exact mathematical wording was checked in the primary PDFs. The target file remains identical to the specified commit.
